column1: dialogue;"
Chaonan: ...Best if you say the bare minimum to me. I don't want to deplete my stamina.
Chaonan: *sigh* If I'd known this would happen
column2: I would have followed my dreams...

column1: Traveler: Are you tired?
Chaonan: ...I'm a ship repairman. When the ships are at sea
column2: I have nothing to do. But when they dock
column3: I'm so busy I never get a wink of sleep...

column1: Chaonan: So I have decided to conserve my stamina from now on. Otherwise
column2: I won't be able to cope when the busy period hits.

column1: Traveler: Have you considered a change of occupation?
Chaonan: Well
column2: this job is rather busy
column3: but being busy also means that there's money to be made.

column1: Chaonan: We have Rex Lapis' divine predictions to thank for that. The number of merchants going out to sea has increased year on year in recent times
column2: which has led to our business being on the rise
column3: too.

column1: Chaonan: Those merchants who made their fortune aren't stingy
column2: either. They often give us some tips on top of the repair fees.

column1: Chaonan: Hard work begets an equal reward
column2: and for the lads that want to earn some money while they're young
column3: this job is pretty good. We shouldn't waste the opportunity that Rex Lapis has given us.

column1: Traveler: What dreams?
Chaonan: ...I once had the opportunity to join the Crux Fleet
column2: but by the time I signed up
column3: they were full.

column1: Chaonan: I gave up on being a seafarer in the end
column2: and went into ship repair work instead. Now I can only watch as the ships go in and out.

column1: Chaonan: Maybe if I'd pushed a little harder for it back in the day
column2: I wouldn't have ended up where I am now.

column1: Chaonan: And maybe the reason I've not been favored enough to receive a Vision is because I give up too easily.
Chaonan: ...I hope you don't end up like me.
Traveler: What a pity...
Chaonan: The problem is my personality... That
column2: and luck not being on my side.

column1: Chaonan: *sigh* It's funny
column2: you know
column3: the day before I signed up I even made a point of going out and buying this feather
column4: which is supposed to bring good luck. Clearly
column5: it had no effect whatsoever...

column1: Chaonan: ...Well
column2: no use complaining about it. Here
column3: you can have it
column4: maybe it works better on adventurers.

column1: Traveler: Goodbye.
Chaonan: Goodbye. Now to focus all my energy on getting a good rest...
";"Traveler:
Hey there! I couldn't help but notice you're working on that old ship repairer's gear. What made you choose this path?
Chaonan:
Yeah

column1: Chaonan:

column1: dialogue;"
Soraya: ...How many secrets does Liyue truly hold?
Traveler: Secrets?
Soraya: Oh
column2: Traveler
column3: it's you. The secrets I'm referring to are a set of inscriptions.

column1: Traveler: Do you mean buried treasure?
Soraya: Haha
column2: who knows? It's always possible. Talk of secrets waiting to be uncovered does tend to make one think of buried treasure.

column1: Soraya: This place we are in is called the Guili Assembly. According to Liyue folklore
column2: it was once inhabited by people — in fact
column3: it was rather prosperous.

column1: Soraya: But for various reasons
column2: the whole place was wiped out. All that remains now is the countless ruins scattered across the landscape.

column1: Soraya: Some stories put it down to conflict between the gods
column2: other people say it was a war between humans. And some sources talk of a sudden
column3: catastrophic natural disaster...

column1: Soraya: Whatever the reason was
column2: ruins are all that remains here now. The only ones who come here are the hilichurls
column3: the Treasure Hoarders...

column1: Soraya: ...And masochistic scholars
column2: like me
column3: who in spite of all the risks just can't resist the idea of how much research value these ruins have to offer.

column1: Soraya: In practice though
column2: scholars like me aren't cut out for this kind of field work! I've hardly covered any ground yet
column3: and I already need a rest...

column1: Soraya: The actual ruin-exploring seems more your area of expertise. What do you say
column2: fancy helping me out?

column1: Traveler: Sure.
Soraya: Great. Hmm
column2: but I should give you an idea of what to look for... Yes
column3: keep your eyes peeled for stone pillars and stone tablets.

column1: Soraya: Given how ancient these ruins are
column2: any text we can hope to find will be written on stone
column3: not paper.

column1: Soraya: After all
column2: stone is the oldest and most durable medium for written communication.

column1: Traveler: What am I looking for?
Soraya: Hmm... Text essentially. Written messages from the past.
Soraya: And if you're looking for text in ruins as ancient as these
column2: that means looking for stone pillars and stone tablets.

column1: Soraya: Stone is the oldest
column2: most durable medium for written communication. All the more so in the domain of the Geo Archon.

column1: Soraya: The stones here have borne witness to all of history. I am sure they will not disappoint.
Traveler: Only if there's treasure...
Soraya: Whatever treasure you find
column2: you can keep. Material wealth isn't what appeals to me.

column1: Soraya: In Liyue there's a saying that goes: ""Money belongs to the world outside your head."" I'm more interested in acquiring knowledge than money.
Soraya: So while you're hunting for treasure
column2: please also keep your eyes peeled for stone pillars and stone tablets.

column1: Soraya: Given how ancient these ruins are
column2: any knowledge we can hope to find will most likely be written on stone.

column1: ";"Here is the dialogue for starting a quest about searching for relics in ruins:

column2: artifacts
column3: and even magical energies that can provide insight into Liyue's most pivotal moments. They're crucial for our understanding of the world we live in.

column1: Traveler: I see. But aren't there others searching for these relics? Treasure Hoarders
